quote: I think around you know, I'm out of town. I'm in Mexico. So I need to look that up.
stewart_read: Customer cannot give a firm bill amount and is traveling, which foreshadows the later bill-document problem. This is the first sign the booking will be conditional rather than clean.
coaching_implication: Rep should flag this early travel/access complication as a risk factor for the appointment rather than let it surface again passively at bill-collection near the end of the call.

stewart_read: Customer doesn't understand the credit score question and the rep offers only a one-line repeat rather than clarifying what it means or why it matters.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally keeping this brief since it's not a closer-tier discussion, but the customer's confusion was never actually resolved.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly clarify credit score context (e.g., 'the number you'd see on a credit report') so the qualifier answer is more reliable than a guess.

stewart_read: The customer's qualifying answer to the hard credit gate is a hedge, not a confirmation, yet the rep accepts it at face value and moves on immediately.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally not pressing since the closer's credit pull will be the real gate, consistent with Spencer's operator note that stated credit is unreliable anyway.
coaching_implication: Flag that this qualifier was never firmly established — the appointment is riding on a guess, and the closer should know the credit answer was soft.

quote: one of the main requirements for getting solar in Colorado is having a credit score above 650
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold rather than the schema's documented 670. This matches a prior observed instance of the same drift on this floor.
coaching_implication: Flag for reconciliation with Kenny on which number is current policy — this is not evidence of the real floor, just a repeat of a discrepancy worth resolving centrally.

quote: And then are you able to get access to your utility bill?
stewart_read: The rep raises the bill only after scheduling is already settled, and does so as a logistics question rather than tying it back to the customer's stated motivation of saving money.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have sequenced this deliberately last since scheduling was the priority given the customer's imminent travel, which is a reasonable call-flow choice.
coaching_implication: Encourage tying the bill ask back to the customer's own 'saving some money' reason to make the request feel purposeful rather than purely procedural.

quote: Why are you interested in looking into it?
stewart_read: Customer gives a real (if brief) reason — economy, climate, and saving money — but the rep doesn't expand on it or use it later when discussing the appointment or bill.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to echo back specific language like 'saving money' when discussing the bill or the appointment purpose, reinforcing the customer's own stated motivation.

quote: I'll just shoot you a text. I mean, my name, and then I'll send my email as well if that's easier.
stewart_read: The rep promises a text/email but never runs the full button-up (no one-hour block statement, no 'is that fair' handshake, no explicit recap of the appointment time before ending).
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close with the full button-up sequence — restate day/time, set expectations for the call, and get a verbal confirmation — rather than ending on a logistics note about the bill.
